CHACHA20_ROUNDS's CHACHA20_QUARTERROUND(st[i],st[j],st[k],st[l]) macro invocations expand to direct compound assignments on the substituted arguments (A += B; D = ROTL32(...); ...), i.e. st[0] += st[4] etc. -- st is genuinely written on every call. pure_permute_args's body explicitly does '/* LINTED const cast */ ((char **) nargv)[pos] = nargv[cstart];' -- nargv (already declared char * const *, i.e. an array of const pointers) is deliberately cast away to permute the pointer array in place; genuinely modified, and the existing cast is the documented reason it isn't already const.
pure_parse_long_options only reads nargv[pure_optind++] to fetch an option argument string; never writes to nargv or through it; static/internal, no ABI constraint.
g_opendir only reads pglob->gl_flags and calls through pglob->gl_opendir; never writes any pglob field; static internal helper, no external ABI.
g_lstat is the same shape as g_opendir -- only reads pglob->gl_flags/gl_lstat, never writes.

fakestat's st is passed straight to the libc stat(file, st) / stat(curdirtmp, st) calls, which write the struct stat fields through that exact pointer -- st is genuinely modified (by an external call the checker doesn't trace as a write-through), and stat()'s own prototype does not accept a const struct stat * either.
fakelstat is the identical shape to fakestat -- st is passed to lstat(file/curdirtmp, st), which writes into it; lstat()'s own prototype requires non-const.

clearargs() itself never writes argv, but stashes 'argv0 = argv;' into a global that setprocessname() later uses to overwrite the string content in place (memset(argv0[0],...); strncpy(argv0[0], title, ...); argv0[1] = NULL;) -- argv's pointee is genuinely modified via that global alias (capturing it for exactly this purpose is the whole point of clearargs), and constifying argv would break the argv0 = argv assignment (argv0 is a plain char **) without a cast.

ulhandler_handle_commands only reads ulhandler->tls_clientfd/clientfd; every other state change in the function (deferred_quit, etc.) is a separate global, not a field of *ulhandler; genuinely never modified.

sc_special_handler's user_data is explicitly cast to void (unused), but the function is registered as a SimpleConfConfig's special-handler callback of type SimpleConfSpecialHandler (a fixed function-pointer typedef, src/simpleconf.h, assigned at ftpd.c:5578) -- the signature can't be independently const-qualified without breaking that typedef match; matches this dataset's already-established fixed-callback-signature FP class (e.g. curl's nghttp2-callback precedent).

storage_port() deliberately returns a non-const 'in_port_t *' alias into *ss (there is already a separate storage_port_const() returning a const pointer for read-only callers) -- constifying ss would force the return type const too, breaking the function's entire purpose as the mutable accessor; not cleanly implementable.
storage_port6() is the same shape as storage_port -- deliberate mutable-accessor twin of storage_port6_const().
storage_sin_addr() is the same shape -- twin of storage_sin_addr_const().
storage_sin_addr6() is the same shape -- twin of storage_sin_addr6_const().

generic_parser's walking cursor config_keywords_pnt (initialized from config_keywords, advanced via config_keywords_pnt++) writes '*config_keywords_pnt->value = strdup(linepnt)' back into the array config_keywords points to -- genuinely modified through a derived cursor alias, not a clean const target.

privsep_privpart_bindresport writes STORAGE_PORT6(query->bindresport.ss) = htons(...) / STORAGE_PORT(query->bindresport.ss) = htons(...), which expand to *storage_port6(&query->...ss) = ... / *storage_port(...) = ... -- a direct write into query's own memory through the mutable ipstack.c accessors; genuinely modified.

strip_lf does 'f = strchr(str, ...)' (a pointer into the same string str points to) then '*f = 0;' through it -- strip_lf's entire purpose is to strip trailing CR/LF in place; str is genuinely modified.

add_new_pw_line's fp2 is passed directly to fprintf(fp2, ...), which mutates the FILE object's internal buffer/position state through that pointer; fprintf's own prototype requires a non-const FILE *, so 'const FILE *fp2' would not even compile.
displayquota only ever reads quota_ ('quota = *quota_;'); the only pointer written is '&quota', a distinct local variable, not quota_ itself; genuinely const-able.

session_ticket_cb is registered via SSL_CTX_set_session_ticket_cb(tls_ctx, NULL, session_ticket_cb, NULL) -- its signature is fixed by OpenSSL's own callback API, not this codebase; const isn't independently applicable to one parameter of a library-mandated callback.
session_ticket_cb's session parameter is the same OpenSSL-fixed-callback-signature shape as tls_ctx above.
session_ticket_cb's arg parameter is the same OpenSSL-fixed-callback-signature shape.

c comes from readchar(), which returns either EOF(-1) or '(int) c' where c is a local unsigned char -- i.e. readchar()'s result is always in {-1} union [0,255]. EOF is excluded by the 'if (c == EOF || ...) return -1;' guard three lines above, so at '*filepnt = (char) c;' c is provably in [0,255] -- a byte value, matching this project's own already-established 'byte values 0-255' non-representation-dependent FP category (e.g. delta-adjudication-task757-sample's INT16-C rows in this same project).
